column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew ends with singular from it; BSB uses plural from them.
The Hebrew repeats hand and Hazael; BSB combines the hands and uses his for the second Hazael reference.
The Hebrew names the face of the LORD and repeats the oppression root; BSB uses favor and condenses the oppression description.
The Hebrew says from under the hand of Aram, names their tents, and compares yesterday and the day before; BSB uses power, homes, and as they had before.
The Hebrew has a singular walking verb and singular in it; BSB makes the walking plural.
The Hebrew uses an active leaving verb with an unnamed subject and says people; BSB says Jehoahaz had no army left.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says they buried him actively; BSB expresses burial passively.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says Jeroboam sat on his throne; BSB describes succeeding him on the throne.
The Hebrew explicitly mentions his face and uses singular chariotry; BSB says over him and uses plural chariots.
The Hebrew leaves the bow-taker unnamed; BSB supplies Jehoash.
The Hebrew leaves the first speaker and hand-placer unnamed; BSB supplies Elisha and the king.
The Hebrew names Elisha only at the shooting command; BSB supplies his name for all three speech introductions.
The Hebrew leaves both speech subjects unnamed; BSB supplies Elisha twice.
The Hebrew does not explicitly repeat the ground or add only to the final three times; BSB supplies both.
The Hebrew describes the raiders coming at the coming of the year; BSB says every spring. It describes burial actively, where BSB uses a passive.
The Hebrew leaves the buriers unnamed and describes the dead man living actively; BSB supplies the Israelites and uses passive was revived.
The Hebrew says all the days of Jehoahaz; BSB says throughout his reign.
The Hebrew says He was unwilling to destroy them and separately states He had not cast them from His face. BSB places both destroying and casting under His unwillingness.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the earlier city-taker and the later defeated man unnamed; BSB supplies Hazael and Ben-hadad.
